learn.hook: 'When I grow up, I will...' Finish that sentence! Today we learn how to talk about the future.
points: We use 'will' + the base verb to talk about the future: I will become a doctor.
'will not' can be shortened to 'won't': I won't give up.
'going to' shows a plan: I am going to learn the tabla.
We can share dreams with 'want to' or 'would like to': I want to be a pilot.
Every dream needs effort today: practise, read and keep asking questions.

example.q: Change to the future: 'Asha paints a picture.'
steps: To talk about the future, use 'will'.
After 'will', use the base verb: paint, not paints.
example.answer: Asha will paint a picture.

learn.reallife: On New Year's Day, many people say what they will do in the coming year. These are plans for the future!

learn.hook: Clink, clink! Glass bangles shine at weddings and festivals. But how does hard glass become a round, sparkly bangle?
points: Firozabad, a city in Uttar Pradesh, is famous for its glass bangles.
Glass is melted in a very hot furnace until it becomes soft.
The soft glass is shaped into coils, cut into rings and joined with heat.
Then the bangles are polished, painted or decorated.
Many skilled people work on each bangle, step by step.

example.q: Read: Zoya's family makes glass bangles in Firozabad. Glass is melted in a very hot furnace, so Zoya watches from a safe distance. Her uncle shapes the soft, glowing glass into long coils. The coils are cut into rings, and the ends of each ring are joined with a small flame. Then Zoya's mother paints tiny flowers on them. 'Each bangle carries the work of many hands,' she says proudly. What happens to the glass after it is shaped into coils?
steps: Find the line about coils: 'The coils are cut into rings'.
Then: 'the ends of each ring are joined with a small flame'.
example.answer: The coils are cut into rings, and the ends of each ring are joined with a small flame.

learn.reallife: When you see a box of shiny bangles at a fair, remember: many artisans worked with great care and skill to make them.

learn.hook: A potter turns mud into pots. A weaver turns thread into cloth. Artisans have magic in their hands!
points: An artisan is a skilled worker who makes things by hand.
A potter makes pots from clay. A weaver makes cloth. A carpenter works with wood.
A blacksmith makes tools from iron. A goldsmith makes jewellery from gold.
India has many famous crafts: Madhubani paintings from Bihar, wooden toys from Channapatna in Karnataka, blue pottery from Jaipur.
Handmade things take skill, time and patience, so we should value them.

example.q: Fill in: 'A ___ shapes wet clay on a wheel to make diyas and pots.'
steps: Think: who works with clay?
A person who makes pots is a potter.
example.answer: potter

learn.reallife: At Diwali, we light clay diyas made by potters. At a crafts fair, you may see weavers, painters and toy makers at work.

learn.hook: One bangle, two bangles... one box, two boxes... one child, many children! Let's learn how words change from one to many.
points: Most nouns add -s to show more than one: bangle-bangles, toy-toys.
Words ending in s, ss, sh, ch or x add -es: bus-buses, glass-glasses, brush-brushes, box-boxes.
Words ending in a consonant + y change y to i and add -es: city-cities, baby-babies.
Many words ending in f or fe change to -ves: knife-knives, leaf-leaves.
Some words change completely or not at all: child-children, woman-women, tooth-teeth, sheep-sheep.

example.q: Make plural: 'The artisan painted one glass and one box.' Change to many.
steps: 'Glass' ends in ss, so add -es: glasses.
'Box' ends in x, so add -es: boxes.
example.answer: The artisan painted many glasses and many boxes.

learn.reallife: At the bangle shop: 'Two dozen bangles, please, in two boxes!' We use plurals every time we shop.

games.title: How do we make it plural?

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'glass'?
quiz.explain: 'Glass' ends in ss, so we add -es: glasses.
quiz.mistake: Uses an apostrophe to make a plural

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'box'?
quiz.explain: 'Box' ends in x, so we add -es.
quiz.mistake: Adds only -s to a word ending in x

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'city'?
quiz.explain: City ends in a consonant + y, so change y to i and add -es.
quiz.mistake: Keeps the 'y'

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'toy'?
quiz.explain: 'Toy' ends in a vowel + y, so we just add -s.
quiz.mistake: Changes y to i after a vowel

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'knife'?
quiz.explain: 'Knife' changes f to v and adds -es: knives.
quiz.mistake: Just adds -s to a word ending in fe

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'child'?
quiz.explain: 'Child' changes completely: children. It already means many, so never add another -s.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s to an irregular noun

quiz.q: What is the plural of 'sheep'?
quiz.explain: 'Sheep' stays the same: one sheep, ten sheep.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s to every noun

quiz.q: Which sentence uses the plural correctly?
options: The womans are painting the bangles.

The womens are painting the bangles.
The woman are painting the bangles.
quiz.explain: The plural of 'woman' is 'women', and it goes with 'are'.
quiz.mistake: Adds -s to an irregular plural

teach.nudge: How do we change a word to mean more than one? What about words like child or leaf?
